title: Plain pages load fast
text:
A page of text needs very little to look good: a sensible font stack, a comfortable line length, enough spacing, and colours with good contrast.

Perfection is achieved, not when there is nothing more to add, but when there is nothing left to take away.
— Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

title: smol
text:
A small, fast HTML format for Quarto websites and documents. It leaves out Bootstrap, Quarto’s JavaScript and icon fonts, and keeps listings, RSS, citations, cross-references, callouts and margin notes. Pages are many times smaller, and show their content sooner on a phone.
Install the extension in your project’s folder:
Then set the format in a website’s _quarto.yml, or in a document’s front matter:
smol reads Quarto’s usual options, such as website.navbar, page-footer, toc and the callout options. Switching an existing site can take two more changes:
What smol does with ordinary Quarto content, with Quarto’s default options. Pages are light or dark following the reader’s system setting; there’s no toggle. The article shows scholarly front matter, citations and the margin.
Body text should be easy to read for a long time. This paragraph has bold, italic, struck out, small caps, H2O, E = mc2, inline code, a link to another page, an external link and a link to a heading. Keyboard keys: Ctrl-Shift-PCtrl-Shift-P.
A second paragraph shows how paragraphs follow each other. Long words and URLs must wrap instead of widening the page: Donaudampfschifffahrtsgesellschaftskapitänswitwe, https://example.org/a/very/long/url/that/goes/on/and/on/without/any/natural/place/to/break/it.

On this page, footnotes go at the end, Quarto’s default.1 The article puts them in the margin.
Each cell is what the page downloads, then how long it takes to show its main content. Downloads are HTML, CSS and JavaScript (gzipped), and fonts, measured with Quarto 1.11.9. With normal Quarto, pages with math also download MathJax’s fonts, which aren’t counted. Times are to the largest contentful paint on a mid-range phone with slow 4G, from Lighthouse 13’s mobile settings (as in PageSpeed Insights), median of three runs, measured on 2026-11-25. Lighthouse rates every smol page 100 for performance. Normal Quarto runs 105 KB of JavaScript on a plain blog post; smol runs none.

title: Small pages for scholarly writing
text:
Introduction
Literate programming mixes code and prose (Knuth 1984). Cohen (1994) criticised significance testing, and others argued for looking at the data first (Tukey 1977; Tufte 2001, 13).

A margin note. On phones it sits below the paragraph it belongs to.

This article sets reference-location: margin, so footnotes go in the margin next to the text that refers to them.1 An aside can be written inline. An aside, written inline in the paragraph.

1. A footnote in the margin.

Methods
We model the outcome as a straight line plus noise, Equation 1:
yi=β0+β1xi+εi,εi∼𝒩(0,σ2)(1)
y_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_i + \varepsilon_i, \quad \varepsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2)
 \qquad(1)
Theorem 1 bounds the mean.

Theorem 1 (Arithmetic and geometric means) For non-negative numbers aa and bb, a+b2≥ab\frac{a + b}{2} \geq \sqrt{ab}.

title: Simple models first
text:
Fit the simple model first:
fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)
coef(fit)
What it misses
Ask what the simple model misses. The model is mpgi=β0+β1wti+εi\text{mpg}_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{wt}_i + \varepsilon_i.
